rules.title: Potential hard-coded credential
rules.remediation: Move credentials to a protected secret store or environment-based configuration, and rotate any real credential.

rules.title: Private key material in source
rules.remediation: Remove the key from source control, revoke or rotate it, and load it from a protected secret store.

rules.title: Dynamic code evaluation
rules.remediation: Avoid evaluating untrusted text as code; use a constrained parser or explicit operation mapping.

rules.title: Subprocess uses a command shell
rules.remediation: Pass an argument list with shell=False and validate each argument; avoid building commands from user input.

rules.title: Unsafe pickle deserialization
rules.remediation: Do not deserialize pickle data from untrusted sources; use a data-only format and validate its schema.

rules.title: Potentially unsafe YAML loading
rules.remediation: Use yaml.safe_load for untrusted YAML, or explicitly configure a safe loader.

rules.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
rules.remediation: Keep certificate and hostname verification enabled; fix the certificate chain instead of bypassing validation.

rules.title: Weak cryptographic hash
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256 or a modern password-hashing scheme as appropriate; MD5 and SHA-1 are not suitable for security decisions.

rules.title: Potentially unsafe HTML insertion
rules.remediation: Prefer textContent or a vetted HTML sanitizer when inserting data that may contain user-controlled content.

rules.title: Potential unparameterized SQL query
rules.remediation: Use parameterized SQL queries instead of interpolating values into query strings.

rules.title: Unsafe C/C++ string function
rules.remediation: Use bounded operations and validate buffer sizes; prefer safer abstractions such as std::string where practical.

rules.title: C/C++ shell execution
rules.remediation: Avoid passing constructed strings to a shell. Use a constrained process API with fixed executable and validated arguments.

rules.title: Potential dynamic SQL concatenation
rules.remediation: Avoid constructing executable SQL with string concatenation; use parameterized statements and validated identifiers.
